US consumers just keep on spending.

US retail sales rose +1.2% in August, the largest monthly increase since March. 

At the same time, retail sales excluding autos increased +1.4%, the 2nd-biggest monthly increase since January 2023.

Furthermore, control-group sales, which feed into the GDP calculation, surged +1.4%, the largest monthly increase since September 2024.

Meanwhile, retail sales adjusted for inflation rose +0.8% MoM in August, to a record $231.6 billion.

Since January 2026, real retail sales have risen +$6.7 billion, or +3.0%.

The US consumer is still spending despite inflation.

Databricks' @alighodsi on the clock that's forcing cyber and data into the same market:

"It used to be like, okay, we have data and AI... you have a bunch of data and you run AI and machine learning, and that just lives separately."

"And then you have the cyber world. Cyber world is, you know, we want to detect if bad people are trying to hack us."

"But now on the data and AI side, we have agents running internally in the company. And the agents are also doing things with other people's agents, and they're producing a lot of data. Logs, trails, fingerprints that are being left."

"All the data that's being produced needs to be analyzed. And the scale at which you need to do that is many, many orders of magnitude more than just one or two years ago."

"2018, 2019, the time it would take from a CVE, a vulnerability being published, until you see it actually weaponized in the industry would be like two, three years."

"That went down in 2022 significantly, but it was still like eight, nine months. So that's kind of fine, you have eight, nine months."

"Now if you look at this curve from 2022 until now, it's down to basically hours, basically no time. Things get immediately weaponized."

@alighodsi

Investors are becoming extremely bearish:

53.3% of individual investors expressed bearish sentiment over the next 6 months in the AAII survey for the week ending September 17th, the highest reading since May 2025.

Bearish sentiment has risen +15.7 percentage points over the last 2 weeks, the largest 2-week increase since March 2026.

Meanwhile, just 28.8% of individual investors were bullish over the same period, the lowest reading since September 2025.

As a result, the bull-bear spread is down to -24.5 percentage points, the widest gap since the first week of May 2025.

This is also comparable to readings seen during the March-April 2025 pullback and the 2022 bear market.

Are we setting up for a short squeeze?

Databricks' @alighodsi and a16z's Martin Casado on where the AI risk is, and what's unfolding in the cyber space:

Martin: "When the internet came out, by this point... we'd disabled hospitals, we'd taken out critical infrastructure, we'd caused tens of billions of dollars in economic damages from worms. All of that had already happened."

"AI has so many people that want to find risks and threats. We're running so fast, so much money has been poured into it, and we haven't seen anything commensurate with the early days of worms. What is that disconnect?"

Ali: "I am sleeping well at night, and I don't think there's existential risk right now. I do think there's a lot of infrastructure that needs to be secured."

"You used to have these SOC teams, security operations center people, that would look at what intrusions are happening, how are we being attacked. And now the humans just can't keep up."

"The whole cybersecurity space is transitioning into being fully automated, using agents for detection."

"If we don't do that, I do think you will start seeing those kind of things, like sites going down, whole systems that stop working for a while. And there will be consequences, not existential, but economic damage and people getting hurt."

@martin_casado

Four year cycle lows are not an exact science. 

Sometimes it’s a little earlier than normal, sometimes a little later.

The idea that the 4 year cycle “failed” despite Bitcoin dropping below the 200W moving average in H2 of the midterm year seems wrong.

The SPX would often bottom in October, but occasionally it would occur earlier (May) and sometimes later (December)

With Bitcoin, the winning strategy has typically been to just DCA in the second half of the midterm year rather than try and time the exact bottom (something I have reiterated multiple times).

tweets.text:
What if, the 4yr cycle is nothing more than a simple and appealing idea, but one that has always been highly coincidental and non-driving?

Thus applying any rules and expectations to it is just fiddling around with a broken concept in an attempt to pretend it ever worked at all.

There are mechanics of markets (internal/external conditions, capital flows and investor behaviour) which actually drive markets.

Studying those, in my opinion, showed fairly clearly when the bottom had formed. Bottom formation started in Feb, and ended in August. Humans are herd animals in markets, and we tend make the same decisions given similar stimulus over and over as a result. Same capitulation events, similar duration, and massive capital changing hands, just like to prior market lows.

Leave the 4yr compass behind, the calendar never created the price, investors making decisions and capital changing hands does. When the investor data tells you the bottom is in, then check the price and the calendar, not the other way around.
